questions.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently
questions.question: What is BM25's characteristic failure mode?
options: Relevant documents sharing no query terms score as irrelevant
Exact identifiers blur into a generic semantic neighborhood
Approximate search occasionally misses a true nearest neighbor
Rare terms receive almost no weight relative to common ones

questions.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently
questions.question: What is dense retrieval's characteristic weakness?
options: Paraphrased natural-language queries fall out of the ranking
Ranking requires labeled relevance judgments at query time
Exact identifiers blur into generic semantic neighborhoods
Documents are scored only by raw term frequency and length

questions.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently
questions.question: For the query `error 0x80070057 windows update`, which retriever should win and why?
options: Dense search, because error text is conceptual
BM25, because the rare exact token dominates the ranking
Dense search, because embeddings store error codes exactly
BM25, because it ignores document frequency entirely

questions.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently
questions.question: BM25 alone reaches recall@100 of 0.85 and dense search 0.82, yet their union reaches 0.93. Why does the union beat either system?
options: The fused scores are better calibrated than either input
The dense model was fine-tuned on this labeled query set
The union removes the irrelevant duplicates from both lists
The two systems fail on largely different sets of documents

questions.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently
questions.question: A BM25-only service adds dense retrieval. Which query segment should improve most?
options: Paraphrased conceptual questions with no shared terms
Exact part-number lookups for items such as ZX-4817-Q rev 3
Windows error-code searches typed verbatim by users
Rare proper-noun queries naming one specific person

questions.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently
questions.question: Why does the query `treatments that do not involve surgery` defeat both a sparse and a dense retriever?
options: Both systems need negation examples labeled at training time to work
The inverted index has no way to store a negated term at all
BM25 counts surgery as evidence and the vector averages negation away
Embeddings match only documents that hold every query term already

questions.topic: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
questions.question: With smoothing constant k, what does a document at rank r in one list contribute to its RRF score?
options: 1 divided by (k plus r)
1 divided by (r squared)
k divided by (k plus r)
1 divided by (k times r)

questions.topic: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
questions.question: What information does RRF take from each retriever?
options: The calibrated relevance probability of each document
The raw score of each document after normalization
The score magnitude and the mean of the whole list
The rank position each document holds in its list

questions.topic: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
questions.question: With k = 60, what is the RRF contribution of a document at rank 1 in one list and absent from the other?
options: About 0.0164
About 0.0323
About 0.0610
About 0.1640

questions.topic: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
questions.question: With k = 60, document A ranks 1st and 6th in two lists while document B ranks 2nd in both. Which fuses higher and why?
options: A, because a single rank 1 dominates the fused score
A, because its mean rank across the two lists is lower
B, because two strong ranks outweigh one top rank
They tie, since both sum to exactly the same fused score

questions.topic: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
questions.question: What is the effect of raising the RRF constant k?
options: It sharpens the advantage held by the very top ranks
It flattens rank contributions toward a plain vote count
It weights the stronger retriever more heavily than the other
It caps how many ranked lists the fusion can accept

questions.topic: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
questions.question: When is weighted RRF justified over plain RRF?
options: Whenever one system's scores are heavy-tailed
When the constant k has already been swept on labels
When one retriever answers with much lower latency
When labels show one retriever is reliably stronger

questions.topic: Score Normalization vs Rank Fusion
questions.question: BM25 returns a top score of 25 with a next-best score of 9 for a query. What does min-max normalization do to that list?
options: It spreads the remaining scores evenly across the range
It centers every score on a mean of zero for that query
It compresses the rest of the list into the bottom of the range
It converts each score into that document's rank position

questions.topic: Score Normalization vs Rank Fusion
questions.question: Why is rank fusion invariant to score scale?
options: Any monotone change to the scores leaves the ranks untouched
It recomputes the corpus statistics once for every query
It normalizes each score by the document's length first
It fits weights that absorb each system's own scale

questions.topic: Score Normalization vs Rank Fusion
questions.question: When can score fusion beat rank fusion?
options: When no relevance labels exist anywhere for tuning at all
When component models are swapped out frequently
When the score distributions are heavy-tailed
When the scores carry calibrated probability meaning

questions.topic: Score Normalization vs Rank Fusion
questions.question: Why is thresholding on min-max fused scores unsound?
options: Thresholds require scores to be integer valued
The fused scale differs from query to query
The fusion weights depend on the threshold chosen
Min-max subtracts the mean from every score

questions.topic: Score Normalization vs Rank Fusion
questions.question: Three months after fusion weights were fitted, an embedding model upgrade silently degrades merged quality. Rank fusion is immune to this because...
options: it refits its own weights on a nightly schedule
it draws far more candidates from each of the systems
ranks hold steady when a score distribution shifts
it normalizes by z-score rather than by min-max

questions.topic: Score Normalization vs Rank Fusion
questions.question: Why do mature pipelines fuse candidates with RRF yet let a trained reranker set the final order?
options: RRF cannot merge more than two ranked lists at a time
The reranker runs without an accelerator at that stage
Fused ranks are a required input feature for the reranker
The reranker scores on one self-contained internal scale

options: Rerank, fuse, retrieve in parallel, then filter the survivors
Parallel retrieval, RRF fusion, filter and dedupe, then rerank
Retrieve, rerank each source, then fuse the rescored lists
Fuse both sources, retrieve, filter, and rerank the result

Replay the last fused ranking that the system had produced

questions.question: Why must multi-tenant ACL filters live inside the retrievers rather than after fusion?

ACL metadata cannot survive the rank fusion step at all
Filtering after fusion doubles the RRF smoothing constant
Retrievers cannot reach the document text any other way

questions.question: For which system is the full Atrium pattern most likely overkill?
options: A stream of heterogeneous natural-language questions
A corpus whose size roughly doubles every month

questions.topic: The Atrium Pattern: BM25 + Vectors + RRF + Reranker
questions.question: Why are per-source ranks preserved through the pipeline?
options: They are needed to compute each BM25 term score
They serve as the fusion weights for the merge
